Quick triage update (initial findings):
- Root cause signal: batch sizing heuristic regression introduced in last rollout (commit 4f7a2c). The heuristic now groups longer sequences together which increases end-to-end latency for those requests.
- Secondary effect: KV-cache thrash. Because larger batches include more distinct prefixes, our in-memory KV cache is getting evicted rapidly; miss rate spiked from 6% -> 48% in the last 20m. That increases decoder time and causes queue growth on the inference workers.
- Symptom mapping: queue growth -> worker saturation -> 429 backpressure from router -> client retries -> retry storm -> upstream timeouts/504s.

Immediate mitigation plan (actions I'm executing now):
1) Roll back the batching heuristic to v3.2 (rollback initiated: rollback-id rb_20270215_1006).
2) Disable autobatching at the request router for the affected customer shard (toggle set to OFF).
3) Trigger KV-cache warm restore and bump cache size on the us-east pool (commands in attachment).
4) Apply short-term rate-limiter at the edge to reduce retry amplification (reduces RPS by ~15% temporarily).

Attaching error logs and a diff of the suspected config change: err_log_20270215.txt, trial-config-diff.patch.

ETA: I expect measurable reduction in 5xx/429 within 20–30 minutes after rollback + cache warm. Will post follow-up with metrics.
